I farm 9 mu with a wheat-maize rotation, and I have a well, so I will keep the full 9 mu in the same system this year. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I need stable yield from a small farm and I cannot afford weak emergence or low production. Since I have farmed for many years and only have two people in the household, I will keep the management practical and familiar rather than complicated. I will use rotary tillage because it fits my scale, saves labor, and works well for preparing land between the two crops.

For wheat, I will put in moderate fertilizer and irrigate three times because in my conditions water at key stages is worth it, especially with well access. I will control diseases and aphids with two pesticide applications if needed, because protecting the stand is important for a good grain fill. For maize, I will invest a bit more in nitrogen because maize responds strongly to it on my land, and I will irrigate twice to support establishment and grain filling. I will use two pesticide applications there as well, mainly to avoid yield loss from common insect and disease pressure. My goal is not extreme input use; I will aim for steady, dependable output from all 9 mu.
